body: The spec's core scientific claim — that topology alone predicts transfer — is undermined by its own simulation design. The policy heads are indexed by platform_id, so the adapter can succeed by implicitly re-deriving the platform label from structural features rather than demonstrating that topology carries transferable behavioral priors. A trivial platform-classifier would pass SC-003 without supporting the research question; the spec needs a control where the adapter is denied platform-correlating features, or an evaluation on held-out platforms. Second, the 'structural ambiguity' handling (FR-008c) excludes or flags exactly the cases where structure fails to predict outcomes — this post-hoc censoring inflates R²/SC-001 and would manufacture the paper's headline '>70% of variance' result. Third, SC-005 is written so that either outcome satisfies it ('yield p < 0.05 to indicate a statistically significant difference (or confirm non-significance)') — it is not a criterion at all. Fourth, FR-002 hard-codes AUC ≥ 0.80 as a MUST for a functional requirement, conflating an empirical hypothesis with a buildable function; the model either achieves this or the project fails, which no engineering process can guarantee. Finally, FR-009's ≤5% degradation budget on synthetic graph variations is circular: it is guaranteed only if the assumption that structural features are layout-invariant holds, and passing the test cannot distinguish genuine robustness from features that were resolution-invariant by construction (e.g., tree depth).
